title: Domain gate fails OPEN on an empty host: _host_matches('','') is True, so a SecretRef with an empty-string domain releases the real secret for an unparseable destination
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:61-63 _host_matches; :105-118 resolve never rejects host=='' from host_of(). Probe: SecretStore(proj(domains=['']),{'PW':'supersecretvalue'}).resolve('{{SECRET:PW}}','') returned 'supersecretvalue' with no exception. host_of() returns '' for any unparseable url_or_host, and SecretRef.domains (schema/project.py:22) has no validator rejecting '' entries.

title: guard_prompt does NOT raise on a raw secret value shorter than 4 characters, and Redactor does not mask it — B2's 'raises rather than being masked-and-sent' is conditional in practice
evidence: src/autotester/core/redact.py:15 _MIN_SECRET_LEN=4, applied in assert_no_raw_secrets():69 and Redactor.__init__():28. Probe: store with {'PW':'abc'}; store.guard_prompt('password is abc') returned normally (no ValueError); store.redactor().scrub('password=abc') returned 'password=abc' unmasked. The length floor is a sensible heuristic for SCANNING unknown text, but these values are known-exact declared secrets — the floor should not gate them.

title: parse_env does not strip trailing inline comments, so 'PW=abc # note' loads the wrong value AND makes the Redactor mask the wrong string
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:36-52. Probe: parse_env('PW=abc # note\n') == {'PW': 'abc # note'}. Consequence beyond a wrong login: redactor() is built from the wrong value, so the real credential 'abc' would appear unmasked in logs and artifacts.

title: Undeclared .env values are absent from the Redactor, so a stray credential in the same file appears verbatim in logs and artifacts
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:100-101 (only declared keys enter self._values) and :134-136 redactor() built from self._values. Probe: .env with STRAY=strayvalue123 -> store.redactor().scrub('log strayvalue123') left it unmasked. B1 correctly refuses to USE an undeclared key; B4 ('masks every secret value in logs and artifacts') argues it should still be MASKED. Note this is a deliberate-looking tension between B1 and B4, not obviously a code bug.

title: SecretStore.load(strict=False) is a security-relevant branch with no test coverage
evidence: src/autotester/browser/secrets.py:82,95. tests/test_secrets.py has 16 tests, none exercising strict=False. Probe confirms the branch fails CLOSED at resolve() (MissingSecret), so this is a coverage gap rather than a live hole — but on the credential boundary the non-strict path deserves an explicit test pinning that behaviour.
